AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. Watering the garden
   B. Adding manure to soil
   C. Planting trees
   D. The washing or blowing away of top soil

2. Why should broken glass be kept out of compost? (1 mark)
   A. It smells bad
   B. It rots too fast
   C. It makes the heap too wet
   D. It does not rot and can cut people

3. Why is a compost heap turned with a fork? (1 mark)
   A. To make it smaller
   B. To remove all the water
   C. To add plastic
   D. To let in air and mix the materials

4. About how long does compost usually take to be ready? (1 mark)
   A. Two years
   B. Ten minutes
   C. Two to three months
   D. One day

5. Which of these helps to prevent soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. Covering the ground with mulch or grass
   B. Digging up all the plants
   C. Burning the soil
   D. Leaving the ground bare

6. How far from the plant should the bottle drip be placed? (1 mark)
   A. Exactly on top of the stem
   B. About 10 to 15 cm
   C. Two metres
   D. In the next field

7. What could a school use to make a simple drip system? (1 mark)
   A. A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   B. A broom
   C. A stone
   D. A wooden door

8. How can a family get firewood without destroying forests? (1 mark)
   A. Cut young trees only
   B. Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
   C. Burn grass
   D. Cut trees from forests at night

9. Which of these makes a scarecrow shine in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Old CDs or shiny strips
   B. Mud
   C. Wet leaves
   D. Soil

10. Which of these is a peaceful way of protecting fruit from birds? (1 mark)
   A. Covering trees with a light net
   B. Setting traps that kill
   C. Poisoning the birds
   D. Burning the trees

11. What is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal kept for milk
   B. An animal kept in a house
   C. An animal sold in shops
   D. An animal that lives freely in nature

12. Why does a scarecrow need a hat and clothes? (1 mark)
   A. To dry the crops
   B. To look like a person and frighten animals
   C. To store food
   D. To keep warm

13. What is a drill in sowing? (1 mark)
   A. A weed
   B. A type of seed
   C. A shallow line in the soil where seeds are sown
   D. A power tool

14. Why do crowded seedlings grow badly? (1 mark)
   A. They like company
   B. They compete for water, light and food
   C. They get too much space
   D. They have no roots

15. Why is it best to plant fruit varieties that suit the local climate? (1 mark)
   A. They cost more
   B. They never get pests
   C. They need no water
   D. They grow and fruit better

16. What do roots of a fruit tree do? (1 mark)
   A. Collect sunlight
   B. Make fruits
   C. Produce seeds
   D. Hold the tree and take in water and food

17. Which sign shows a purple passion fruit is ripe? (1 mark)
   A. Bright green skin
   B. Deep purple skin that begins to wrinkle
   C. Hard green skin
   D. A white flower

18. What is a seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A ripe fruit
   B. A dry stick
   C. A young plant grown from a seed
   D. A type of soil

19. Why is compost mixed into the planting hole? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the hole shallow
   B. It prevents growth
   C. It feeds the young plant and improves the soil
   D. It kills the seedling

20. Which of these completes the farm cycle: animals, manure, ____? (1 mark)
   A. Machines
   B. Bricks
   C. Crops
   D. Roads

21. Why should hands be washed after handling chickens? (1 mark)
   A. To remove germs
   B. To get feathers off
   C. To colour the hands
   D. To warm the hands

22. Why is a meal of only chips not balanced? (1 mark)
   A. It lacks body-building and protective foods
   B. It has no energy
   C. It has too much protein
   D. It has too many vegetables

23. Which of these root foods gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Egg
   B. Sweet potato
   C. Kale
   D. Milk

24. What does proportion mean in a meal? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of the food
   B. The right amount of each kind of food
   C. The price of the food
   D. The number of plates

25. What should you do if oil in a pan catches fire? (1 mark)
   A. Carry the pan outside quickly
   B. Blow on it
   C. Pour water on it
   D. An adult covers the pan with a lid and turns off the heat

26. Why are eggs put in cold water after boiling? (1 mark)
   A. To make them raw again
   B. To cool them so they are easy to peel
   C. To colour them
   D. To make them larger

27. What should you do after coughing into your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Wipe them on your clothes
   B. Wash your hands with soap and water
   C. Shake hands
   D. Ignore it

28. How does the tippy tap release water? (1 mark)
   A. A foot lever tips the container
   B. By a magnet
   C. By a battery
   D. By a switch

29. Why should combs and towels not be shared? (1 mark)
   A. They break
   B. They become dirty faster
   C. Germs and lice can spread
   D. They are too big

30. About how long should you rub hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. Not at all
   B. About 1 second
   C. About 5 minutes
   D. About 20 seconds

31. Why should a rubbish bin have a lid? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavy
   B. To keep out flies and rats
   C. To stop rubbish from rotting
   D. To look pretty

32. Where should you start mopping? (1 mark)
   A. Outside
   B. Next to the door
   C. In the middle
   D. At the corner farthest from the door

33. Why should you never mix cleaning chemicals? (1 mark)
   A. They become soap
   B. They will cost more
   C. They can give off harmful fumes
   D. They will look nicer

34. What is personal protective equipment? (1 mark)
   A. Clothing and gear worn to protect the body
   B. Food for health
   C. Tools for digging
   D. Soap for cleaning

35. Which PPE protects the body and clothes from dirt? (1 mark)
   A. Canvas shoes
   B. Dust mask
   C. Gloves
   D. Overall

36. What should you do with laces when cleaning canvas shoes? (1 mark)
   A. Remove and wash them separately
   B. Cut them
   C. Burn them
   D. Leave them dirty

37. In even tacking, the stitches and gaps are (1 mark)
   A. The same length
   B. Absent
   C. Different lengths
   D. Very long

38. What is a tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. A cutting tool
   B. A temporary stitch that holds cloth in place
   C. A type of cloth
   D. A permanent decorative stitch

39. About how long is each stitch in even tacking in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. 1 cm
   B. 10 cm
   C. 1 metre
   D. 1 mm

40. Where should needles be kept? (1 mark)
   A. In your mouth
   B. On the floor
   C. In a pin cushion or needle case
   D. On a chair

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Give three benefits of eating a balanced meal. (3 marks)

42. Give three uses of sheep. (3 marks)

43. Name three foods that are boiled. (3 marks)

44. Explain how mulch and compost help a young fruit tree. (4 marks)

45. Describe how to make a bottle drip for one plant. (3 marks)

46. Name three safety rules when using gas for cooking. (3 marks)

47. Give three times when you should wash your hands. (3 marks)

48. How can a school without land grow radish or amaranth? (3 marks)

49. Write the steps for preparing a meal using both boiling and shallow frying. Include hygiene and safety. (5 marks)

50. A family boils beans for a long time on a big fire with the lid off. Suggest five ways to improve fuel use. (5 marks)

51. Explain two mistakes that can spoil a newly planted fruit tree and how to avoid them. (4 marks)

52. Give three peaceful ways of protecting crops from birds and animals apart from a scarecrow. (3 marks)

53. Explain four ways in which wild animals help people or the environment. (4 marks)

54. Give two advantages of boiling food. (2 marks)

55. Name four fuels used for cooking in homes. (2 marks)

56. Explain how compost conserves both soil and the environment. (5 marks)

57. Explain what is wrong with a meal of ugali and salt only, and how to improve it. (3 marks)

58. Why should fruit be washed before it is eaten? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — The washing or blowing away of top soil
   Bare soil can be carried away by rain or wind.

2. D — It does not rot and can cut people
   Glass never rots and can injure anyone handling the compost.

3. D — To let in air and mix the materials
   Mixing brings outer material to the middle so all rots evenly.

4. C — Two to three months
   It depends on weather and materials but is usually two to three months.

5. A — Covering the ground with mulch or grass
   Covering keeps rain from washing soil away.

6. B — About 10 to 15 cm
   Close enough for the roots to reach the water.

7. A — A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   A bottle with small holes in its cap drips slowly.

8. B — Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
   Growing trees keeps a supply of wood.

9. A — Old CDs or shiny strips
   Shiny objects flash and scare animals.

10. A — Covering trees with a light net
   A net keeps birds away without harming them.

11. D — An animal that lives freely in nature
   Wild animals are not kept by people.

12. B — To look like a person and frighten animals
   Animals fear people, so a figure like a person scares them.

13. C — A shallow line in the soil where seeds are sown
   A drill is a shallow furrow made with a stick.

14. B — They compete for water, light and food
   Too many plants in a small space fight for resources.

15. D — They grow and fruit better
   Wrong climate gives poor growth.

16. D — Hold the tree and take in water and food
   Roots anchor and absorb.

17. B — Deep purple skin that begins to wrinkle
   Purple types change colour when ripe.

18. C — A young plant grown from a seed
   A seedling is a young plant.

19. C — It feeds the young plant and improves the soil
   Compost gives food and helps water retention.

20. C — Crops
   Manure feeds crops, and crops feed animals.

21. A — To remove germs
   Poultry can carry germs.

22. A — It lacks body-building and protective foods
   Chips give mainly energy.

23. B — Sweet potato
   Sweet potatoes are starchy.

24. B — The right amount of each kind of food
   Proportion means the right amounts.

25. D — An adult covers the pan with a lid and turns off the heat
   Water makes an oil fire worse.

26. B — To cool them so they are easy to peel
   Cold water stops cooking and cools the eggs.

27. B — Wash your hands with soap and water
   Germs from coughs stay on hands.

28. A — A foot lever tips the container
   Pushing the lever tips the container.

29. C — Germs and lice can spread
   Personal items should be for one person.

30. D — About 20 seconds
   This is long enough to clean properly.

31. B — To keep out flies and rats
   Lids stop pests.

32. D — At the corner farthest from the door
   You do not step on the clean floor.

33. C — They can give off harmful fumes
   Mixing chemicals is dangerous.

34. A — Clothing and gear worn to protect the body
   PPE protects us from harm.

35. D — Overall
   An overall covers the body.

36. A — Remove and wash them separately
   Laces need to be washed too.

37. A — The same length
   Even tacking is equal.

38. B — A temporary stitch that holds cloth in place
   Tacking is removed later.

39. A — 1 cm
   Even tacking uses 1 cm stitches and gaps.

40. C — In a pin cushion or needle case
   Needles are sharp.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives energy, helps the body to grow and repair, and protects from illness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mutton, wool (some breeds), skins, manure, income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes, eggs, cassava, maize, beans, rice (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mulch keeps the soil moist, reduces weeds and protects roots from heat. Compost feeds the tree and improves soil structure.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for mulch, 2 marks for compost.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make tiny holes in the cap, fill the bottle with clean water, bury the neck upside down near the plant, press soil around it and refill when empty.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for holes in cap, 1 mark for placing near plant, 1 mark for filling and refilling.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep the cylinder upright and away from fire; close the valve after use; if you smell gas open windows and do not light a flame.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before eating, after using the toilet, after playing outside, after touching animals, after coughing (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a box or tin with drainage holes filled with fine soil and compost; sow the seeds thinly; water gently and place in sunlight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for container, sowing, care.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands; wash food; boil potatoes until soft; shallow fry an egg or fish; serve with vegetables; safety: adult present, handles inward, dry cloth, water away from hot oil; clean up after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for hygiene, 1 for boiling, 1 for frying, 1 for safety, 1 for serving and cleaning.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Soak the beans first, cook with the lid on, use dry wood, reduce the flame after boiling starts, cut food or use an improved jiko, put out the fire after cooking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Burying the graft joint under the soil, plant with joint above the ground; not watering in dry weather, water regularly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake and 1 for each solution.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Nets, fences, noise makers, shiny objects, guarding at the time animals come (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Birds eat insects; bees pollinate; animals spread seeds; wildlife brings tourists and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: It needs no oil and it makes hard food soft and safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Firewood, charcoal, gas and kerosene.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each fuel, total 2.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: It adds food to the soil and makes it firm so it is not washed easily. It reuses wastes instead of leaving them as rubbish, and it reduces the need for factory fertiliser.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for soil, 2 marks for environment, 1 mark for a clear example.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: It only gives energy. Add beans or fish for body-building and vegetables or fruit for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for problem, 1 for protein addition, 1 for protective addition.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remove dirt and germs so it is safe to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for germs or safety.
